edits.name: Happy in the parents' group chat: answers when named
edits.description: Happy joins one three-way iMessage group with both parents and answers when addressed by name, so both see the answer. The group helper answers from weather and web search only: it keeps no memory and has no calendar, list, mail or note tools. M1 signed off iMessage groups as disabled; this re-opens them for that one chat, which Tony approved on 12 Oct.
edits.example: In the parents' group Jordan writes: 'Happy, will it rain on Saturday afternoon?' and both parents see the answer. A message in the group that does not name Happy gets no reply.
edits.how: A parent creates the three-person group from a phone; Tony reads its chat id with `imsg chats`. Config: `channels.imessage.groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, `groupAllowFrom` with the parents' handles, one `groups[<chat_id>]` entry with `requireMention: true`, and a binding with `peer.kind: "group"` that routes that chat to a new shared, memory-less group agent generated from the family file: `web_search` and `home_weather` only, memory search off, no accounts, no hand-off, its own capped model key. Mention patterns come from the agent's name. `channels.imessage.historyLimit: 0`, so skipped messages are not handed to the helper when it is next named. Go-live gate: both parents write three messages that do not name Happy, then one that does; Tony reads that turn's session record. If a parent's own agent answered, or any of the three messages is in the record, the group stays off. Not built: the group as a target for scheduled texts. No house-rules rule.

Tony provides a new capped model key for the group helper at execution (the roadmap's rule: one capped key per agent)

The go-live gate passes: the message that names Happy is answered by the group helper and not by a parent's own agent, and with the group history limit at 0 that turn holds none of the messages that did not name it
caveats: This changes the M1 baseline, which keeps iMessage groups disabled: one registered chat is admitted, with a sender allowlist and answering only when named. Every other group stays ignored.
In Basic mode Happy can read and reply in a group but has no group actions such as renaming it or adding people, so a parent creates the group from a phone.

Both parents see every answer given in the group, so nothing from one parent's notes, mail or calendar belongs there; the group helper holds none of it and cannot be asked for it. Who is in the chat is decided on the parents' phones: the sender allowlist stops anyone else from being answered, not from reading the answers.

Left at its default, a group that answers only when named hands the helper up to 50 skipped messages the next time it is named, which would send the parents' own conversation to the cloud model beside web search results. The history limit of 0 is what prevents that, and it is untested on iMessage, hence the go-live gate.
The group is not a place for scheduled texts: a scheduled job delivers only to its owner, so something meant for both parents is two jobs, one each.
Each parent can already ask the same weather or web question one to one; the gain is one shared answer that both see.
edits.safety: The group helper is a separate shared agent with no memory, no accounts and no calendar, list, mail or note tools, so nothing one parent's agent holds can surface in front of the other. The gateway, not the model, admits only the parents' handles and the one registered chat; the helper has no message tool and replies only there. Search results are outside content.

edits.description: Once a day a script with no model looks 14 days ahead: when an event on the family's shared Google calendar falls at a time when both parents' own calendars show busy, each parent who has it switched on gets one line naming the event and the time, once, ending with a plain 'Who covers?'. Happy only reports: it moves and declines nothing, and it does not carry the answer between the parents.
edits.example: Trigger: the daily check finds a family-calendar event next Thursday at 4 pm while both parents' own calendars show busy. Each parent gets, in their own thread: 'Thursday 22 October, 4:00 pm: [the event's title]. Both of you show busy then. Who covers?' The same clash is not reported again.
edits.how: One no-model command job (`--command-argv`) per parent who has it switched on, Tony's first, created by the jobs script (G003), once a day in the morning at an hour Tony names at execution. A host script lists the family calendar's events for the next 14 days, asks for both parents' busy times (`gog calendar conflicts` or `freebusy`), compares against its own seen-list state file and prints one labelled line per new clash, or `NO_REPLY`. Each job delivers only to its owner. Sign-in, the plan's default: each parent's job uses that parent's own read-only calendar sign-in (F009), and the other parent shares their own calendar with it as 'See only free/busy'; no script loads two people's sign-ins. Tony confirms this at execution. Personal events appear only as 'busy'; only family-calendar titles are named. 'Who covers?' is plain text: no relay, no record of the answer. No rule decides which events count: every such overlap is reported.
depends_on: F009 read-only calendar sign-in on the family's shared Google calendar, with gog installed: Tony's for his job, Jordan's own for hers
G003 in its simplified form: the jobs script creates the command jobs, one per parent who has it switched on
Each parent shares their own Google calendar with the other parent's account as 'See only free/busy'
Tony provides at execution: the hour of the daily check, which calendars hold each parent's own appointments, and his confirmation of whose sign-in reads them
caveats: An overlap is not always a problem (both parents at the same recital). With no rule for which events count, the watch will sometimes flag one that needs no cover.

The watch sees only calendars shared with the sign-in that reads them. A work calendar counts only if it is a Google calendar and the employer lets its busy times be shared outside the organisation; otherwise that kind of clash is missed unless the parent blocks the time on their own calendar.
Happy reports; it does not move or decline anything, and it does not pass one parent's answer to the other.
Each parent's line comes from that parent's own job. Jordan's job needs her own calendar sign-in, which she approves herself on Google's screen.
It runs once a day, so a clash created after that day's run is reported the next morning.
No Google or Apple help page was found that describes a warning when two people's calendars clash, so this looks like a gap the phones leave open; that is the absence of a finding, not proof.
edits.safety: No model call, so text in event titles cannot steer anything. The calendar grant is read-only. The script asks only for busy times on the parents' own calendars, so one parent's private event titles are never shown to the other; only shared family-calendar titles appear. Each job texts only its owner, and no sign-in is used outside its owner's job.
unverified: Flags and output of `gog calendar conflicts` and `freebusy`: gog is not installed, only its command list page was read.
Whether those commands work on a calendar shared as free/busy only, and under the read-only calendar grant that F009 sets up.

Where each parent's own appointments live, work included: an employer's Google calendar can be shared outside the organisation only as far as its administrator allows, and a work calendar that is not on Google cannot be read at all.
That a command job run by the gateway can use the calendar sign-in stored for F009's server: not tried.

tony_provides: The hour of the daily check (a morning hour)
Which Google calendars hold each parent's own appointments, work included, and each parent switching on busy-only sharing
His confirmation of whose sign-in reads the calendars (the plan's default: each parent's own calendar sign-in, with the other parent's busy times shared to it)
new_risk: a host script that uses a parent's calendar sign-in; each parent's busy times shared with the other parent's account
check_note: No change of substance: the text now says Tony's job comes first and Jordan's is a second job when she has it switched on, and the safety text says the script asks only for busy times.

edits.name: Day-out and trip planner: options with the weather and links
edits.description: 'Plan Saturday for us, rain likely' returns two options, each with the forecast for home, links, opening hours where a page that could be read shows them, and an admission price only when a page that was read showed one. A weekend or longer plan comes back the same way, with hotels and transport as links, not prices. The parents book; Happy books and pays for nothing.
edits.example: Tony texts: 'Plan Saturday for us, rain likely.' Happy sends two options, one indoors and one outdoors with a rain fallback, each with Saturday's forecast, a link with the time the page was read, opening hours where the venue's page showed them, and the admission price where it showed one.
edits.how: A short planning rule on each parent's agent and on the research helper (F019), plus one hand-off with a time limit. The helper searches and reads venue pages; the forecast for home comes from the existing `home_weather` tool on the parent's agent. The answer gives two options with the weather, links and their fetch times, opening hours where a page that could be read shows them, a price only from a page that was read, and nothing booked. The task handed to the helper carries only a place, a distance, dates and the children's ages; never names or the school. Dates come from the parent's request, so no calendar read is needed. Not built: the place lookup with its Google Cloud project, key and wrapper, the Friday text, the paperwork line for trips abroad, a house-rules rule. Before go-live: one eval case (a price only from a fetched page) and one live request whose record shows what went to the helper.
depends_on: F019 research helper live: it does the reading, after the outbound proxy is built and after its own test that a hand-off returns the answer in the same chat
home_weather plugin (exists)
Tony provides the two children's ages at execution (their grades are on record, their ages are not): typed into the family file with the other family facts, or given in the request
caveats: Happy books and pays for nothing: the plan ends in links and the parents book.
Prices are best effort. Plain page reads fail on many booking, hotel and transport sites, so those come as links, and an admission price appears only when a page that could be read showed it.

There is no place lookup, so opening hours come only from venue pages that could be read, with no ratings and no drive time; for 'is it open now?' the maps app on the phone is quicker. A place lookup is a later add-on: the roadmap names Google's hosted Maps server, it needs billing switched on, and that has not been put to Tony.
What reaches the research helper (a place, a distance, dates and ages) is an instruction to the parent's agent, not an enforced limit.

A long plan comes back as a text; once 'email me this' (F049) is live it can be emailed to the asker like any other long answer. The forecast is the one for home, in half-day periods; an hour-by-hour rain line needs the hourly forecast (F083).
A general assistant such as Gemini already drafts an itinerary from a typed prompt. What this small version adds is the forecast for home in the same answer and arrival in the iMessage thread.
edits.safety: The research helper holds no family data and has no payment or booking tool; it is given only a place, a distance, dates and ages, never names or the school (a prompt rule, checked on one live request's record, not an enforced limit). Web pages are outside content, and the helper's answer is treated as untrusted. Answers go only to the asking parent.
unverified: Hotel and train price snapshots: no opened source shows these sites are readable logged-out; expect links instead of prices.
That a hand-off to the research helper returns its answer in the same chat: the roadmap lists this as not yet confirmed on this version, and it is F019's first test.
The weather plugin returns 12-hour periods today (read in the config repo, not citable), so an hourly rain window needs the plugin change in F083.
